services.name: IAuditService
methods: log(action, resourceType, resourceId, actorId, oldValues, newValues)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Foundation — leave-type, audit, employee
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency leaf modules. leave-type is a pure enum with no dependencies. audit is a standalone infrastructure concern (GP-002). employee provides identity and manager lookup needed by all other modules. These must exist before anything else can be built.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Policy layer — leave-policy
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on leave-type and audit (both in Phase 1). Defines entitlement rules, accrual rates, and approval requirements that leave-balance and leave-validation consume.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Balance engine — leave-balance
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-policy, employee, leave-type, and audit (all in Phases 1-2). Tracks entitlements, used days, remaining days per employee per leave type per fiscal year. Provides deductBalance and restoreBalance used by leave-request workflow.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Validation & notification — leave-validation, notification
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-validation depends on leave-balance, leave-policy, leave-type (Phases 1-3). notification depends on employee (Phase 1). Both are consumed by leave-request in Phase 5. Can be built in parallel.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Orchestration — leave-request
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior phases. Orchestrates the full leave workflow: submit (validate → deduct → audit → notify), approve/reject (update status → audit → notify), cancel (restore balance → audit → notify). Exposes the public REST API via controller and routes.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries

- **Domain layer** (innermost): leave-type (enum), leave-policy model, employee model, leave-balance model, leave-request model + LeaveStatus enum, audit model, notification model. No dependencies on services or infrastructure.
- **Application layer**: Service interfaces + implementations. leave-request orchestrates the full workflow; leave-validation enforces rules; leave-balance manages entitlements; leave-policy provides rule lookups; employee provides identity/manager resolution; audit logs all state changes (GP-002); notification sends alerts.
- **Infrastructure layer**: Repository interfaces + implementations (one per domain model). All DB access through repositories (GP-001). Shared DB connection at `src/shared/db/connection.ts`.
- **Presentation layer**: Controllers + Fastify routes. Only leave-request, leave-balance, and leave-policy expose public REST endpoints. All endpoints enforce RBAC (GP-005) and validate inputs at boundaries (GP-003).

## Key design decisions

- **leave-validation is a separate module** (not embedded in leave-request) so validation rules can be reused and tested independently.
- **leave-balance is a separate module** (not embedded in leave-request) because balance tracking has its own lifecycle (accrual, fiscal-year rollover) independent of individual requests.
- **leave-type is a leaf module** containing only the enum — no service, no repository. It is the single source of truth for leave type values consumed by policy, balance, validation, and request modules.
- **Audit is cross-cutting**: every state-changing operation in leave-request, leave-balance, and leave-policy writes an audit record via IAuditService.log().
- **Notification is fire-and-forget**: leave-request calls notification after state transitions but does not depend on notification success for the core workflow to complete.
- **Manager resolution**: leave-request uses IEmployeeService.getManagerForEmployee() to determine who should approve. The employee module owns the reporting hierarchy.

## REST API surface (exposed by leave-request controller)

- `POST /api/leave-requests` — submit (employee)
- `GET /api/leave-requests/:id` — get by ID (employee/manager)
- `GET /api/leave-requests/employee/:employeeId` — list by employee (employee/manager)
- `GET /api/leave-requests/manager/:managerId` — list for manager (manager)
- `PATCH /api/leave-requests/:id/approve` — approve (manager)
- `PATCH /api/leave-requests/:id/reject` — reject (manager)
- `PATCH /api/leave-requests/:id/cancel` — cancel (employee)

## REST API surface (exposed by leave-balance controller)

- `GET /api/leave-balances/:employeeId` — list balances (employee/manager)
- `GET /api/leave-balances/:employeeId/:leaveTypeId/:fiscalYear` — single balance (employee/manager)

## REST API surface (exposed by leave-policy controller)

- `GET /api/leave-policies` — list active policies (authenticated)
- `GET /api/leave-policies/:id` — get policy (authenticated)
- `POST /api/leave-policies` — create (HR admin)
- `PUT /api/leave-policies/:id` — update (HR admin)
